q: A three-phase charging station draws a current of $16\,\text{A}$ from each phase conductor, and the phase voltage is $230\,\text{V}$. How large is the charging power?
a: Each phase transfers a power of $UI$, so $P = 3UI = 3 \cdot 230\,\text{V} \cdot 16\,\text{A} = 11\,040\,\text{W} \approx 11\,\text{kW}$.

q: A battery has to be charged with $45\,\text{kWh}$, and the efficiency of charging is $90\,\%$. How much energy is taken from the grid?
a: $W_\text{grid} = W_\text{battery} : \eta = 45\,\text{kWh} : 0.90 = 50\,\text{kWh}$. More is taken from the grid than is stored in the battery, because part of the energy turns into internal energy of the cables, the charger and the battery.
